raw_response:
I'll reason through my year as this farmer, then lay out my plan.

---

*Let me think about this year...*

I'm 65 now, been farming this land outside Quzhou for 30 years. My son works in town at a factory, my daughter-in-law helps me with the菊花 (chrysanthemum) picking in autumn, and the grandkids are in school so I can't count on them except during summer break. My wife still helps with field work but her knees aren't what they used to be. So labor is tighter than the 7 people on our household book suggests.

Of my 20 mu, I keep 15 mu in the wheat-maize rotation — that's my grain, my food security. The other 5 mu I put into chrysanthemum because the buyer from the cooperative gives a decent price and it brings cash in autumn when the maize money is already spent. I won't expand the chrysanthemum more than that — too much hand labor for an old man.

**Wheat** (already planted last October, harvesting in June): I used the 济麦 variety that my neighbor老王 recommended three years back and it hasn't failed me. Put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg/mu of 15-15-15. I'll topdress urea at green-up in March — maybe 15 kg of urea per mu. Some younger farmers do two topdresses now but I've always done one big one and it's fine. Irrigation: winter water in December (already done), green-up water in March, then once at grain filling. Three times. Extension station told us about a new fungicide for 赤霉病 (scab) — I'll spray once around heading if the weather is humid, otherwise skip it to save money.

**Maize** (June after wheat harvest — turnaround is brutal, maybe 5-6 days): I use 郑单958 or whatever hybrid seed the agro-dealer has fresh. Straw from the wheat gets crushed and left on the field — I don't have time to do anything else. Base fertilizer goes down with the planter, then one topdress of urea at big flare stage (大喇叭口). If it doesn't rain in July I'll run the well once — pumping is expensive so I don't irrigate unless the leaves curl. I expect around 500 kg/mu, could be 550 if the rains cooperate.

**Chrysanthemum**: This is the fussy crop. I planted cuttings from my own patch last spring — no need to buy seedlings. I'll put down more fertilizer here because the buyer pays by flower weight and quality. More urea and compound fertilizer, and I'll topdress twice. Irrigation from the well when it's dry in July-August. Aphids can be a problem so I spray insecticide two or three times in summer. Harvest is all by hand, late October into November — my daughter-in-law and I will manage, and if it's too much I'll pay a few女工 by the day.

Cash is tight this spring because fertilizer prices went up again. I might buy slightly less compound and rely more on urea at topdress — cheaper per unit of nitrogen.
